newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk shares rally 2.46 pct to new record.
newsitem.headline: Turk shares rally 2.46 pct to new record.

text.p: Istanbul shares rose in firmer volume and selective trade led by state-owned stocks on Thursday as the market targeted the psychological barrier at the index's 2,000 level amid persisting political optimism, brokers said.

The IMKB National-100 closed at a new all-time high of 1,999, up 48 points, or 2.46 percent from Wednesday and compared to a previous record close of 1,953 on Monday. But it fell from a trading high of 2,010 it brushed in late trade.
Brokers said the stock market was considered as the most attractive investment area amid falling interest rates and strong expectations for a stable dollar/lira rate.
They say the investors are also confident that political turmoil eased on increased hopes that the new coalition government would win a key parliamentary confidence vote on Saturday.
"Today's rise was fuelled by technical reasons after the index had broke its resistance at 1,950 with an increasing trade volume," said one broker.
He said speculation that more MPs would resign from opposition True Path Party to support the government also boosted stock prices.
Murat Aysen from Finans Securities said strong buying activity emerged in the afternoon session after demand for state owned flat steel producer giant Eregli picked up.
"This had fuelled the market and the buying spree ran its course until the end of the day," he said.
The trade volume jumped 31.6 percent to 35.76 trillion from yesterday's 27.18 trillion.
Top actives of the day were Eregli, up 1,500 at 26,000, Akbank down 250 lira at 11,500 and Tupras down 1000 lira at 97,000.

Of the 247 shares traded, rises outdid the falls 140 to 54 while 53 were unchanged. The IMKB Industrial gained 3.02 percent to 1,879, the IMKB Services inched up 1.79 percent to 1,936 and the IMKB Financial leapt 1.26 percent to 2,170.
The metals sector was the leading gainer with a 5.58 percent premium.
